Applicant must hold an unexpired NCARB certificate for registration without further examination; alternatively, a combination of education, experience, and examination endorsed by NCARB and approved by the board.

Applicant must hold a substantially similar license in good standing in another state, territory, or district of the United States; license must not have been revoked for bad faith or ethics violation; applicant must not hold suspended or probationary license; must be sufficiently competent; and pay any required fee.

Must hold a valid license, registration or certification from another state, territory, district, possession, or a country participating in the applicable profession's national council mutual recognition agreement, AND hold a certification or model law designation from the applicable profession's national council.

The board may grant eligibility through NCARB-accepted programs; military spouse applicants may receive expedited licensure and temporary licenses under general Department of Consumer Affairs provisions.

Must hold a license in good standing in another jurisdiction with substantially equivalent qualifications; submit application in form prescribed by the board; may use a national clearinghouse designated by the board.
NCARB certificate, or evidence of registration in a state with substantially equal requirements plus at least 10 years of practice in that state.

Applicant must qualify to take the prescribed examination and have passed it or a substantially equivalent examination in another jurisdiction and satisfied the internship requirements; or hold a valid license from another U.S. jurisdiction with substantially equivalent criteria; or have passed the prescribed examination and hold a valid NCARB certificate with a valid license from another state. Applicant must hold a current NCARB certificate and a current certificate of registration in good standing from another jurisdiction.

Applicant must hold a current license from another state issued under requirements of a standard accepted by the board, and the person's record must fully meet the requirements of this state in all respects other than examination.

Applicant must be a licensed architect in another state or country where qualifications were equal to Kentucky's at time of licensing, and where reciprocal licensing privileges satisfactory to the board are granted to Kentucky licensees.
